Your VaultInk reader, from the phone

VaultInk is the software on your e-reader that reads your Obsidian Vaults from its SD card. This app is its companion: it talks to the reader over Wi-Fi, so you can send it notes, manage its card and change its settings from the phone.

On the reader, open Transfer & Remotes (File Transfer on older firmware) and pick Join a Network (the same Wi-Fi as the phone) or Create Hotspot (then join the reader\'s Wi-Fi on the phone). Keep that screen open while you use the app.

Note: write a quick note or share text and pictures from other apps. It\'s saved on the reader\'s card right away; with LiveSync set up, the reader also sends it to your other devices on its next sync.
Files: the whole SD card. Upload, download, rename, move and delete.
Settings: Reader setup (Wi-Fi networks, LiveSync, OPDS catalogues, remote servers, fonts) and the reader\'s settings, by category. Changes apply right away.
Convert a comic (in Files): Banana Comic Converter inside the app; the converted comic goes straight to the reader\'s Comics folder.
Bring notes in (in Note): a Google Keep export becomes Markdown notes in your vault.
Type into the reader (in Note): text you write here appears behind a From phone button in the reader\'s next text field. In Home, LiveSync can be asked to sync when you leave Transfer & Remotes.
Help (in the ⋮ menu): VaultInk\'s documentation, offline, with a search.

The app talks only to the reader on your Wi-Fi, and to GitHub when you ask it to check for an update. The comic converter runs from its own website only when you open it. No account, no tracking, nothing sent anywhere else.

The companion app for VaultInk, the Obsidian-vault firmware for the Xteink X4 Pro e-reader. It talks to the reader over Wi-Fi while Transfer & Remotes is open: quick notes and shares into a vault, the SD card, the reader\'s settings, comics, Keep imports and the LiveSync status, from the phone. Free software under the MIT licence.

Found a bug on the reader? A developer build of the firmware and a debug page make a report you can send. The page needs Chrome or Edge on a computer and a USB cable; it does not work on a phone yet. Nothing is uploaded: you save the report and send it yourself.
How to make a debug report (GitHub)
The code of this app is MIT. It includes these libraries:
kos25k: testing on a real reader and the issues that shaped it
CrossPoint Reader: the firmware VaultInk is built on
